title: Token stage atlas and auto-prioritized trace digests
author: Maya Singh
summary: Introduce a token-stage attribution atlas and compact trace digests that auto-prioritize retention by an entropy-weighted signal to reduce storage while preserving investigatability and alert fidelity.
description:
Motivation: Long-tail incidents and cost/latency investigations often require understanding not just per-invocation aggregates but the per-token stage progression (tokenization, encoding, KV-access, self-attention, decode) across the invocation timeline. Full traces are large and expensive to retain; our current sampling misses many subtle degradations that start as stage-level skew. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) a Token Stage Atlas metric and dashboard that synthesizes per-stage timing histograms and stage transition counts per route/model, and (2) a compact Trace Digest format (trace-digest) with an auto-prioritization policy that keeps a small, information-rich subset of spans for long-tail investigation.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a Token Stage Atlas generator that rolls per-invocation phase timings into compact stage histograms and a per-route stage SLI time series. Implements a trace-digest encoder that produces a highly-compressed representation (span-level summaries + token-phase deltas + small KV-hit bitmaps) and a retention prioritizer that scores digests using an entropy-weighted heuristic (combines token-phase variance, error/exception signal, and anomaly score from the local anomaly service). Provides a new dashboard with drilldowns, a synthetic replay hook for reproducing digest-edge cases, and a migration shim so existing downstream consumers can opt into the digest stream via feature flag.

Design notes and constraints: - Trace-digest is intentionally lossy: full spans are not reconstructed; digests are meant for triage and RCA. - Prioritizer runs as a best-effort async op in the telemetry pipeline and is tunable by tenant. Scores are (0.0-1.0) and stored alongside the digest metadata so queries can filter by score. - Atlas histograms are downsampled into exponential buckets to control cardinality while preserving fat-tail detail. - This PR includes a dry-run mode which emits digests and prioritization scores to a side-index (no change in retention) for 7 days to allow ops validation.

Ops runbook highlights (single string): To enable for a tenant: set feature flag observability.token_stage_atlas=true and observability.digest_prioritizer=enabled|dry-run in the tenant console or via the CLI. Dry-run will produce digests and scores but not change retention. Rollout plan: start in dry-run for 48-72h, verify digest entropy distribution on the new dashboard, then enable for 10% of traffic and monitor SLOs and storage delta. If alerts spike, revert to dry-run immediately.
